findings.summary: The committed log's '# revision: 7d09b85b' header names the first commit, but the script committed at 987c54c1 is a different blob (267 changed lines: BOOTSTRAP_ROUNDS 5000 to 2000, plus the LARGE_N Wilson/normal fallback). Re-running the landed script reproduces every number in the log exactly, so the log is accurate for the landed script; the defect is that a reader checking provenance by the header would conclude the log predates the code that produces it and would distrust a reproduction that in fact holds.

The document says the implement/clive pair 'selects 2,865 records across all history'; the committed log prints 2,867 and a re-run of the landed script prints 2,868. The number is context rather than a reported metric, but it is one of the document's own figures that its script does not reproduce.

The moved-boundary control's results are computed into moved_ok and moved_no_change and printed, but neither value reaches verdict_from: only control_ok (the positive control) gates the verdict. If the negative control had reported a detectable difference, the script would still have emitted 'better', which is the case the plan's negative control exists to catch. The control passed on this run, so the recorded output is correct; the instrument does not enforce it.

metric_values publishes '"promoted": len(runs)', which is the analysed-run count labelled as the promoted count. report_window recomputes the promoted total separately, so nothing currently reads this field, but any later caller that trusts it gets a wrong number under a name that looks authoritative.

The section says 'Each estimate carries a 95% bootstrap interval over runs (2,000 resamples)', but the failed-or-aborted request row is a Wilson interval over 141,782 request rows, not a bootstrap over runs; deepseek-1017-on-our-work.py:221 substitutes the closed-form interval above LARGE_N. The method sentence therefore overstates what the bootstrap covers for one row of the table it introduces.
